Based on HeliBoard

The keyboard is theirs: layouts, correction, gestures, themes, dictionaries. This fork adds encryption on top. It is not endorsed or supported by the HeliBoard developers, and problems with this version should not be reported to them.
Plain text is not copied: the chat app could read it from the clipboard. Encrypt first.
Don\'t copy plain text

Copy and cut do not work while you are writing in the keyboard\'s row. Text on the clipboard can be read by the chat app that has focus, and it stays in the phone\'s clipboard history: the same hole that writing inside the keyboard is meant to close. Turn it off and you can copy, but what you copy leaves the keyboard.
Block screenshots

Prevents screenshots, screen recording and the thumbnail Android saves for the Recents screen, on everything that shows decrypted text. When off, the system saves an image of the plain-text message to disk for the recent apps list, and any app that records the screen can see it. Turn it off only if you really need a screenshot.
Open copied messages automatically

When you copy an encrypted message, the keyboard opens it without you pressing anything, even if the keyboard is not on screen. Two things to know, because when it does not work the reason is always one of these. Clipboard history must be on: that is where the text is already read, and reading it on our own initiative would turn the keyboard into an app that spies on the clipboard. And the keyboard must be running: if the phone\'s battery manager stops it, copying does nothing. In that case use the selection: long-press the message and choose “Decrypt”. That path works even when the keyboard is stopped, and it is one step less.

Keep the keyboard alive

Use this only if removing the battery restriction was not enough. It adds a permanent notification whose only purpose is to stop the phone from killing the keyboard: it is the only thing the most aggressive battery managers respect. The cost is that notification in the status bar and the permission to show it.

Forward secrecy

Every message carries a new key, and reading a reply throws the old ones away. Someone who took your phone and your key tomorrow could not reopen what you already sent. The price: an old conversation can no longer be reopened, not even by exporting it. The latest messages stay readable for a while, then they close too as the conversation moves on. Turn it off if you need to be able to reread it. The recipient needs this version or newer, and you must already be among their contacts.
Another %1$s?

You had already called a different key %1$s, and then forgot it. This is another key.\n\nIt can mean two things, and they cannot be told apart from here: they changed phone, or someone else is using that name. The only way to know is to compare the fingerprint with them, in person or over a channel other than this chat.

Burn the conversation
You have forward secrecy on: most of the messages already exchanged with this person are unrecoverable on their own, because they open only once. There is little to destroy here.
Burn the conversation with %1$s?

On this phone it is final: the messages exchanged with this person will never open again, not even for you. The contact stays and you can keep writing to each other: the next message starts from scratch.

A request is copied to the clipboard for you to paste to the other person in the chat: if their app honours it, they delete too. It cannot be enforced: anyone who wants to keep the messages can, and the platform has its own copy of the ciphertext anyway.

The first message you wrote to each other does not burn: when it was sent there was nothing shared yet to destroy.
Burned. The request for the other person is on the clipboard: paste it into the chat.
%1$s burned the conversation. It cannot be reread from here either.\n\nRequest written on %2$s: if this date is very old, someone may have pasted an old request again.
Forget %1$s?

You lose the link between this key and this person. The next message they send will show up as from a never-seen sender and will be stored again without any notice: the same thing you would see if someone were impersonating them. “Compared in person” is lost too.\n\nAbove all: their messages will no longer open. Forgetting also destroys your temporary keys towards them, which are the keys their messages are read with: it is the same property that keeps the past safe, and here you pay for it. Adding them back is not enough, those keys do not come back. To read them again you must write to them first, and it is their reply that will open.
